features.text: The patient is a 74-year-old male.
The patient has a history of rheumatoid arthritis.
The patient has right knee swelling and pain that has been present for about two months and has worsened.
The patient's right leg is swollen, especially around the knee.
The patient's knee pain is usually around a 6 on a normal day but has decreased to a 3 recently.
The patient experiences fatigue on some days.
The patient has not had any fever or weight loss.
The patient has not undergone any recent imaging or blood tests for the leg swelling.
The patient received a steroid injection in the right knee during the last visit.
The patient's right knee feels warm to the touch and has tenderness around it.
The patient has not experienced recent trauma or injury to the leg.
The patient sits for long periods during the day, especially when feeling stiff or in pain.
The patient has not experienced shortness of breath, chest pain, or calf pain.
The patient is taking Xeljanz, 11 milligram dose, daily.
The patient is taking Celebrex, 200 milligrams daily.
The patient has not had any recent changes in RA medications or dose adjustments.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the color of the leg or new symptoms like numbness or tingling.
The patient has difficulty getting up after sitting for a while due to swelling and soreness.
The patient uses a cane sometimes.
The patient has not had any recent blood tests such as CBC, CRP, or ESR.
The patient has not had any recent imaging studies such as an ultrasound or MRI of the right knee or leg.
